h7SylvanAncientTreant.description:
Treants can live for centuries, even millennia. The oldest Treants are slow but resilient, their bodies protected by thick bark hardened over thousands of years. They can also animate the plants around them, turning them into weapons against the enemies of the forest.
Ancient Treants may well be the oldest creatures walking the land of Ashan. If they could talk, they might tell fairy tales! Alas... they only growl and roar.

h7EntanglingRoots.description:
{Entangling Roots}
Hit foes can't move until Treant moves or dies

h7LivingShelter.description:
{Living Shelter}
Defend: +7 Defense, adjacent hexes block foes

bonus.description:
{Siege Shooter}

h7SylvanBladeDancer.description:
The elite of the forest warriors. Elves who devote their lives to the elven martial arts are called War Dancers. They rely mainly on dodging and swift movement rather than toughness or brute strength. Blade Dancers wear no armor, but often tattoo protective magic onto their skin.
The elves have many different kinds of blade dances, and mastering even one of them is a remarkable achievement.

h7Vigilance.description:
{Vigilance}
Can't be flanked or backstabbed by any effect

bonus.description:
{No Retaliation}
Enemy cannot retaliate when attacked

h7SylvanBladeMaster.description:
These warriors learn from the finest swordsmen of Irollan. They move nimbly, like feathers in the wind. In battle, the swordplay of Blade Masters is swift and precise, like leaves in a hurricane, and few survive the flash of their silver blades.
Remember the many blade dances I mentioned earlier? These Blade Masters have mastered more than one.

h7Vigilance.description:
{Vigilance}
Can't be flanked or backstabbed by any effect

bonus.description:
{No Retaliation}
Enemy cannot retaliate when attacked

h7SylvanDruid.description:
Druids are priests of Sylanna, Dragon of Earth. Through her they gain the ability to command all kinds of natural forces, which helps them through all sorts of perils.
Morrin, as they are called in the elven tongue (by MMX's breakdown, meaning “earth song”); the word for druid has no gender in the elven tongue, and all of them are called “druids”, or literally, “those who know plants well”.

cast_h7AbLeafDaggers.description:
{Leaf Daggers}
1/battle: shot pierces line, ignores Defense

bonus.description:
{Siege Shooter}
No damage loss when shooting over walls

h7SylvanDruidElder.description:
Before High King Alaron seized power, the duty of choosing the elven king fell mainly to the Druid Elders, who had to endure in a sweltering sauna until they agreed on who would be the new ruler. That tradition is gone now, but the Druid Elders remain the social and spiritual pillars of elven society.
The Druid Elders' headdresses are not obtained by killing. A stag nearing the end of its life will seek out a druid of its own will and offer its hide, after its death, for the druid to use as they see fit. For a druid, receiving such a gift is a very great honor.

cast_h7AbLeafDaggers.description:

1/battle: shot pierces line, ignores Defense

h7SylvanDryad.description:
When close to death, an elf may ask to be buried in the trunk of a living Treant. Needless to say, this requires a close bond between the elf and the chosen vessel for this rare burial rite to succeed. The tree's living heart wraps the elf's remains, forming the shape of an unborn child. The elf's soul then returns to the world of Ashan as a forest spirit known as a Dryad.
Dryads can sing trees into tools, weapons and even buildings to help their elven kin. A chorus of Dryads can even shape an ancient tree into an elven city.

h7TreantSynergy.description:
{Treant Symbiosis}
It & adjacent allies +9 Defense; heals Treants

h7SylvanEmeraldDragon.description:
As they age, a Green Dragon's scales slowly turn into emerald, until it dies, or rather, until its draconic essence returns to the Spirit World, leaving only an emerald shell in the world of Ashan. Many treasure hunters and adventurers have tried to travel to Irollan in search of these precious shells, but none has ever returned...
Like their ancestor Sylanna, Emerald Dragons are the most patient and unhurried of dragons. Only when provoked do they breathe corrosive gas to dissolve intruders.

breath.description:
{Acid Breath}
Breath attack hits two hexes.

immEarth.description:
{Earth Immunity}
Immune to Earth curses; half Earth damage.

regeneration.description:
{Regeneration}
Top unit heals ${val} HP each round start.

Active hit: 50%, then 25% dmg over 2 rounds.

{No Retaliation}

h7SylvanGreenDragon.description:
As avatars of the Elemental Dragons, dragons come in all shapes and sizes. The scales of young Green Dragons look like stones covered in moss or other plants. Green Dragons are the guardians of earth and nature; they answer the call of the elven war horns echoing through the forest and join in its defense.
Because a Green Dragon's hide is made of rock and covered in moss and all kinds of plants, sleeping Green Dragons are often mistaken for mounds or hills. Their heavy, hoarse breathing, however, serves as a good warning to unsuspecting travelers.

h7SylvanHunter.description: In times of peace, Huntsmen are mainly responsible for feeding the forest communities. They are respected for their superb skill and courage. Huntsmen roam all over Irollan, living in harmony with nature and its many unwritten laws. They never kill needlessly. But in times of war, they feel no regret about using their talents to strike enemies from afar. Some may find it odd that Irollan has Huntsmen, but it is not: elves are not vegetarians, although many druids choose to be.

bonus.description:
{Siege Shooter}
No damage loss when shooting over walls

h7SylvanMasterHunter.description:
Master Huntsmen devote themselves to the defense of the forest realm and will rise to stop any intruder. Their enchanted bows let them loose two arrows before the enemy can react.
A Huntsman earns the title of Master Huntsman through a special ritual in which an Ancient Treant gives the elf a branch taken from its own body, to be carved into a bow. The Master Huntsman uses this bow until the end of his life, and in the end it is buried with him.

h7DoubleShot.description:
{Double Shot}
Kills 1+: shoots again; target may retaliate

bonus.description:
{Siege Shooter}
No damage loss when shooting over walls

h7SylvanMoonDoe.description:
The most mysterious and wondrous creatures one can meet in the forest maze are the Moon Does and Sun Deer, which are in fact two kinds of a species called Twilight Deer. Moon Does are serene and lovely creatures, yet they are still able to protect their fawns from any threat. More than one poacher has met a tragic end at the hands of an angry Moon Doe.
Female Twilight Deer are nocturnal. Although they do not burn to ashes in sunlight as some old nursery rhymes claim, they prefer to come out at night, especially when Asha's moon hangs high in the sky, which is how they got their name.

bonus.description:
{No Retaliation}
Enemy cannot retaliate when attacked

h7SylvanOakDryad.description:
A Dryad's appearance is shaped by the Treant that gave it life, and its body and soul remain closely bound to that Treant. They protect and support each other until the end of their lives. Oak Dryads, born of oak Treants, are stronger and tougher than other Dryads, which makes them good helpers in wartime.
Like spirits, Dryads are very hard to destroy once and for all. I suppose, much like nature itself

h7TreantSynergy.description:
{Treant Symbiosis}
It & adjacent allies +9 Defense; heals Treants

h7GiftOfLife.description:
{Gift of Life}
After acting, Dryad heals also reach adj. Tent

h7SylvanPixie.description:
Flower Sprites are spirits born naturally from flowers, and the scent of the flower stays with them all their lives. The kind of flower determines a Flower Sprite's type, personality and abilities. Flower Sprites are tiny humanoids, no more than a foot tall. Elves enjoy their company, and druids in particular often look after these mischievous little beings.
There are marked differences between Flower Sprites born of wildflowers and those born in flower beds. The former are wilder and more solitary, and die quickly once captured or tamed.

h7SylvanSprite.description:
Sprites usually have brightly colored skin, hair and eyes. Their wings look much like a butterfly's, but actually come from the leaves and petals of the flower they were born from. Their wings let them fly fast and nimbly. In battle, Sprites scatter a pollen called “Pixie Dust”, which makes enemies itch all over, sneeze or cough, leaving them unable to strike back.
Sprites are closely tied to the change of seasons: they are rarely seen in winter, but are relatively numerous in spring and summer.

h7SylvanSunDeer.description:
Male Twilight Deer are diurnal, drawing their power from sunlight. The magnificent antlers of the Sun Deer are shaped like the sun or the stars. Both bucks and does are wondrous creatures, and the Sun Deer radiate a peaceful aura.
Needless to say, mating is a very complicated matter for Twilight Deer, partly because males and females only have a chance to meet during the brief times when the sun and moon share the sky.

h7InspiringPresence.description:
{Inspiring Presence}
Self and adjacent allies +1 Morale, +1 Luck.

bonus.description:
{No Retaliation}
Enemy cannot retaliate when attacked

h7SylvanTreant.description:
Treants are rare and precious forest spirits, usually looking like huge walking trees. As embodiments of nature's fertile power, they are the guardians and caretakers of other trees, plants and flowers. They are natural allies of the elves, and share a unique symbiosis with them: they can rebirth the elves buried in their trunks as Dryads.
Treants are only born in the sacred soil of the deepest parts of the Irollan forest, a land close to the ley lines or dragon veins most attuned to the essence of Earth.
